notes.title: Backer survey #2 highlights
notes.content:
Last week we completed the 2nd backer survey giving everyone who has backed the game on oortonline.com and purchased the game via Steam Early Access an opportunity to contribute and define Oort Online's direction.

Let us start by saying that the data and comments we collect during this process are insanely useful. They often challenge decisions that we thought were obvious, and confirm items that we were unsure of. So if you've taken the time to respond - thank you!!

Firstly the next milestone goal.

[url=http://oortonline.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/vote2-goal.png][img]http://oortonline.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/vote2-goal.png[/img][/url]

We have unlocked this goal and are already making progress towards it. Expect to see some sneak peaks of Character Race developments in the coming days and weeks. We're already exploring what this means.

[h1]Developing a smart feature roadmap[/h1]
In the [url=http://oortonline.com/news-backer-survey-1-highlights/]1st Backer Survey[/url] we wanted to discover which high level features excited the community. This was helpful as it allowed us to really understand the domains that players wanted to see in the future. What was hot? But we didn't really know when players wanted to see them. As the game currently stands the playable features are quite contained as we've been focusing on establishing the core MMO services and game engine. We have received lots of comments encouraging us to rapidly get deeper and more diverse gameplay systems and mechanics into Oort Online. We realised that there were definitely [b]"now"[/b] features that players thought were essential to the core experience [b]today[/b]. Players wanted these essential features to help them spread the news of Oort Online. Likewise, the most exciting features such as "Exploring mines, dungeons, castle, cities, temples", whilst cool - might not be needed instantly - especially if they'll take a considerable effort to deliver.

So where do we focus [b]today[/b]? Which features progress the game the most [b]today[/b]?

Likewise, which features do we believe are essential for a 1.0 release? These features are core to the game. Features that fall after 1.0 are probably nice to have - but not essential.

[i](The items are ordered by a weighting of [2x Now + 1x Before 1.0 - 1x Never]. This allows us to roughly balance the variation in the voting between the different options.)[/i]

[url=http://oortonline.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/vote2-feature-timeline.png][img]http://oortonline.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/vote2-feature-timeline.png[/img][/url]

Now we dive into a little more detail. We know the game will include combat, but what type of combat? We've heard requests for all sorts of styles and required skill levels. Also where is the divide between PvP and PvE? We are currently working on this area.

We already have the predictive logic in place for ranged combat, and we're now exploring how we can populate the worlds with an endlessly varied collection of creatures to challenge, entertain and reward you. Clearly there is also an interest for something where the combat is a little more involved. Maybe you'll think twice about wandering too far without your friends to keep you company? Maybe you'll not dig too deep without being prepared to run home?

[url=http://oortonline.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/vote2-worlds.png][img]http://oortonline.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/vote2-player-combat.png[/img][img]http://oortonline.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/vote2-combat.png[/img][/url]

We also have a fairly regular request for players who want to host, maintain, mod and run their own servers using the Oort engine and server. We've [url=http://oortonline.com/forums/topic/server-hosting/]commented on a few forum posts[/url] in this area and it is definitely part of our plans - we'll share some more information soon.

[url=http://oortonline.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/vote2-worlds.png][img]http://oortonline.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/vote2-worlds.png[/img][/url][url=http://oortonline.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/vote2-servers.png][img]http://oortonline.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/vote2-servers.png[/img][/url]

It's also worth commenting that we realise that the answers to the Vote#2 reflect the wishes of players who have already bought the game. We're not ignoring potential players who haven't bought the game - yet. Understanding why they're holding off or looking elsewhere is also really important. Likewise the feedback we get from the forums, in the Steam community pages, on Twitter and face-to-face at game shows all gets rolling into the decision making process.

Please let us know in the comments if you think there is an area of the game that isn't getting enough attention.

notes.title: Have your say! Early Inventory, Crafting, Beacon GUI designs
notes.content:
[h1]About new GUI[/h1]We've been working on some early (super early) interface designs for the inventory system. The inventory system is probably the most important graphical interface in Oort Online. Core interactions like crafting, buying, claiming, waypoints, guild, friends, selling, trading will all potentially interact with the inventory system. Rather than have boring lists and permissions systems, we're experimenting with something we call Tokens. Everything we're showing below is early, but should give you an idea for the flavour of how interactions will work in the future. We're showing it because we want to know your thoughts, so throw them in the comments or tweet us [url=http://twitter.com/oortonline]@oortonline[/url].

[h1]What are Tokens?[/h1]Tokens in Oort Online are essentially our form of metadata. They refer to players, locations, claims, jobs/stats and currency. Tokens are physical items you can collect that live in a separate inventory style interface, can be stored in chests and even thrown on the ground. You can craft your own player tokens (in my case, 'Ben Tokens') and give them to other players when you meet them. Here's some examples:[list]	[*]Want to add your friend to a Beacon so they can build? Get your friend give you their personal Player Token which can then you put into your Beacon (just like a chest or any other inventory).[/*]	[*]Want to track a location (for example: your home) on your minimap? Craft a Token and put it into your map inventory (again, just like a chest or any other inventory).[/*]	[*]Want to see when your friend comes online? Throw their player token into your map inventory and they'll show up when they're online.[/*][/list]Everything in Oort Online is tangible and can be shared or traded. Focusing on nailing an inventory system should also allow us to keep things simple and familiar. Today we're showing the Crafting and Beacon interfaces.

[h1]Crafting[/h1]We want crafting in Oort Online to be easy, experimental and not require to be switching to a wiki. To make crafting easy and not require the use of a wiki, all players need to do to craft an item is throw items/blocks in the ingredients section and the output will show outputs that can be crafted using those inputs (for example, eggs and flour craft a cake, but eggs, flour and a window will not craft anything). To make crafting experimental, some recipes can be enhanced using a modifier. For example, players may be able to craft a faster pickaxe using topaz as a modifier. The percentage increase in speed is random roll (within some limits) and success can be increased by increasing the amount of Topaz used as a modifier. We'll share more about the crafting and mod system in the future.

[img]http://oortonline.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/Screen-Shot-2014-12-09-at-16.30.20.png[/img]

Here's a bit more detail about the individual components:

[img]http://oortonline.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/crafting.png[/img]

[h1]Beacons[/h1]We don't want players to have to learn new interfaces and concepts every time we add a new feature. The Beacons are a good example where we're using the inventory interaction metaphor ("[u]ooh, fancy design language"[/u]) to manage permissions in a more fun and tangible way. Usually with permissions management you'd find boring check boxes, lists and buttons. Here were using player and claim tokens.

[img]http://oortonline.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/Screen-Shot-2014-12-09-at-16.30.27.png[/img]

Here's a bit more detail about the individual components:

[img]http://oortonline.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/beacon.png[/img]

Now it's your turn: what do you think about these early designs? Comment below, discuss in the forum or tweet us [url=http://twitter.com/oortonline]@oortonline[/url]!

notes.title: Editor Release: 2
notes.content:
New Features:
  * Add button on the base noise nodes to re-seed the individual noise node.
  * Add world seed to editor. Seed is any string value and affects every aspect of generation.

Fixes:
  * Fix some bad cases in blending of 3d biome features.
  * Fix regression in 3d visualisations causing old meshes to not be removed on re-mesh. This was a serious performance killer.
  * Add checks that non-stackable block types like LONG_GRASS or FLOWERS are not used in
    substrate/strata/instances/ores. Remove these block types from the relevant drop-down lists.
  * Fix some inconsistencies in PRNG usage leading to non-deterministic output.
  * Ensure generator produces exact same output across all OS/system library versions... we hope. Let us know if we're wrong!
  * Fix elliptical ore vein nodes not having their state applied on load (Caused them to have their name / collapsed states reset, and to be centred on screen at load).

notes.title: Release: 91 - Lag fixes
notes.content:
New Features:
[list]
[*] Torches no longer prevent water from flowing through them. Torch will disable (particle + light) when approximately under the water.
[*] Add volume 'slider' to options menu.
[/list]
Fixes:
[list]
[*] Fixed a lag issue for Steam client when connecting to servers with pings >100ms.
[*] Fix various issues to do with interacting with the world and your inventory whilst manipulating the inventory, especially bad with larger ping times.
[*] Predict drowning and fall damage fully on client, including death. No more lag on air-meter when going into/out-of water, or weird behaviour where you can run around / place blocks for a short time after dying with no effect on server.
[*] Improved stability of physics when running around over smoothed terrain.
[*] Improved stability of physics when creep-walking into walls previously causing jittering, and for the most part remove glitchiness that caused boosting out of blocks or bouncing back from walls at tops of slopes.
[*] Fix lower level of detail meshes not showing user changes on some worlds.
[*] Server crash fixes.
[*] Fix torches not rendering in some cases. Don't render torch particles if torch is completely surrounded by fully opaque blocks.
[*] Ensure lower-detail chunks do not render torch meshes or particles.
[*] Fix lod'ing issue for liquids.
[*] Fix user edited areas in lod on some older worlds, eg Tawas.
[*] Fix some options like birds not being saved in all cases from options menu.
[/list]

notes.title: Release: 90 - Level of detail updates, fixes and optimizations
notes.content:
New Features:
[list]
[*] Options for EXTREME and ULTIMATE terrain detail levels for screen shots and power users.
[*] Added right click (left trigger or X on controller) to go backwards through a list in the options menu.
[/list]
Fixes:
[list]
[*] Fix lower level of detail meshes not showing user changes. Level of detail chunks with changes may take a while to regenerate.
[*] Fix F12 not taking screen shots on Steam client.
[*] Fix block-lighting updates on chunk deltas for Steam client.
[*] Fix emulated mouse with xbox-pad stopping when stick is not moving even if not at rest state.
[*] Fix new chunks not loading when switching terrain detail.
[*] Improve performance of block lighting for eg, lava oceans.
[*] Fix fogging of sky/sun in reflections causing sky/sun to be always be clearly visible.
[*] Fix cracks in geometry at y = 256 on chunk borders for both web and Steam client.
[*] Fix physics issue (falling through floor with prediction errors) at y = 256 on floating platforms.
[/list]

notes.title: Release: 89 - Lighting balance and full xbox controller support
notes.content:
New Features:
[list]
[*] Add emulated mouse support for xbox-pad. Can use all gui screens with xbox pad now.
[*] Allow game to run whilst in world menu screen.
[*] Make hand held lights twice as bright/far-reaching.
[*] Night time lighting balance - no longer pitch black!
[*] HDR lighting balance - allows for better contrast, less exploded lighting at night.
[*] Fog balance - Sky more visible thanks to clever distance based fog, moodier low-lying fog.
[*] Water balance - water less murky and grey. Now lighter, shinier and wibblier.
[*] Cloud shadows balance - Less intense, no longer casts almost-black shadows
[/list]
Fixes:
[list]
[*] Handle focus and mouse-lock lost correctly in-game, resetting all input when these actions occur to prevent things like running forwards after alt-tab'ing out of the game.
[*] Fix bug in input handling that would sometimes cause events to be handled more than once, should resolve any issues with mouse-wheel scrolling or any remaining instances of locked key/mouse states.
[*] Fix issues with input handling when in chat screen causing locked states.
[*] Fix for blurry loading status text.
[*] Fix black horizontal line appearing in fog on some hardware.
[*] Tweak lighting in LOD so lava is more consistently lit.
[*] Tweak other lights so they are less dark in LOD.
[*] Fix visible halo on sun when fogged.
[*] Optimize lava lighting a bit.
[/list]

notes.title: Release: 87 - Sun, moon and clouds effects polish
notes.content:

[list]
[*] Add option (on by default) to render clouds with soft clipping against world. Will impact performance slightly when enabled.
[*] New sun/moon textures and colours. No more tellytubby sun, and moon is visibly textured.

[list]
[*] Fix fogging of sun and it's god-rays and lens-flare. God rays are much more prominent and not so blocked out by fog now.

[*] Fix the world being darkened when standing around block lights in broad daylight.
[*] Remove the incorrect ping times on the Worlds screen.
[*] Fixes for portal loading.
[*] Reduced brightness of torches closer to that of lamp blocks. Was previously able to light up the world brighter than the sun with just a few torches.
[/list]
